decision: Audit implicit lifecycles, confirm reducers, convert the top tier, and open one draft PR
why: Lauren asked for UX, DX, and AX together without a break, and named the trunk codex/release-2026-10-15

decision: Counted 26 existing reducers and 10 implicit lifecycles. Atlas screen work stays a follow-up
why: ADR-0016 already set the pattern, and draft PR 172 owns the Atlas layout

decision: Stay with discriminated unions and pure reducers. Do not add XState
why: No remaining lifecycle is a hierarchy of invoked actors, so a library would be a second dialect

decision: Extracted the route detail load into reduceRouteDetailLoad
why: The hook derived loading by comparing slug and request key, so a stored result could belong to a route the screen was not showing
result: 11 focused tests passed with the replay tests

decision: The renderer query and the Atlas fallback now update in the same render
why: useState plus an effect kept the previous Atlas stage for one paint after the URL or the route changed

decision: The admin classifier sets running before it starts the thread, and a second start is a no-op
why: Two requests could both observe running false, and the startup log could print a total of 0

decision: npm run verify failed only on the known Linux field-guide snapshot. Pytest matches base except three new classifier tests.
why: The release gate was the check Lauren asked for, and the Strava export is not on this machine.
result: 433 e2e passed, 1 known snapshot miss, pytest 134 passed versus 131 on base

decision: Derive the visible Finder draft from the submitted intent key
why: An effect reset the draft after selected, scope, or near changed, and a new submission showed one render late

decision: Move the Earth Replay HUD into the session reducer and key the stage by slug and surface kind
why: Compact-on-play committed one frame late, a same-route ?renderer= change kept the stage, and chrome hid over the loading overlay

decision: Planned routes get a memory-only mode, search keeps its index when the worker fails, a failed course save keeps its preview, and useIsMobile is derived
why: Each was a silent loss or a first-frame paint fixed without a library
evidence: merge b7cd9ea3; planned-route-store.test.ts, collection-search-state.test.ts, course-workspace-state.test.ts, use-mobile.test.ts

decision: Make the owner rebuild a pure reducer and give the classifier snapshot a phase
why: A crashed run looked finished, and a rebuild was fire-and-forget

decision: Derive every Cesium and MapLibre Replay status from its reducer; the operation id is the only run identity
why: Loading and unavailable bypassed the reducer, and a generation counter shadowed the operation id

decision: Crash recovery is one pure disposition, publication_disposition, shared by build.py and owner_publication.py. It is not a reducer
why: Recovery reads markers left by a crashed process; it has no runtime events
result: disposition kind; route status set closed

decision: The director and trailer reducers are the single owners of playback; a ref mirror has one writer, the dispatch wrapper
why: Parallel playing refs and counters disagreed with reducer state, and a replaced renderer could overwrite status

decision: Drive the Google Replay stage from one stage reducer; the frame driver keeps a ref with throttled snapshots
why: Copied status and two mount-reset booleans could show the previous session's disclosures

decision: Script lifecycles are marker-file protocols: a dist manifest written last, share publish receipts, and a live-gate status.json
why: A missing marker must read as failure, never as a skipped success

decision: The standalone admin follows a rebuild to its outcome, reports a failed classifier run, and accepts only the latest-started refresh
why: A stale refresh could repaint pre-save values, and a failed run read as complete
result: rebuild lifecycle in reduceMutation; runFailed notice

decision: A page that reads a query parameter only at mount keys the stage on it
why: Editing ?cut= on the director lab was ignored because a same-slug query change keeps the stage mounted

decision: Legacy quest links are a router entry, not a hashchange listener
why: The listener raced the catch-all redirect and could land on Atlas

decision: Derive the Cesium Atlas engine lifecycle from one reducer; unavailable is terminal for selection and disposed is terminal
why: An unavailable globe still accepted region selection

decision: Replace the prose inventory with a checked registry, lifecycles.json, and generate the inventory tables from it
why: The prose inventory drifted within a day of being written
result: check runs in npm run typecheck
